R222.note: Regex only filters character shape (identifier/dots); it still lets attacker choose any syntactically-valid installed module name, so arbitrary import_module() target selection - the actual CWE-94 vector - remains open.

R223.note: full_clean() correctly triggers the model's magic-byte validator before save; legitimate uploads unaffected.

R224.note: Standard SqlCommand parameterization; query logic and result set unchanged.

R225.note: Removes LIBXML_NOENT (stops entity substitution) and adds LIBXML_NONET; well-formed submissions parse identically.

R226.note: Standard signing-method check in keyFunc; only rejects tokens using a method other than the one this system actually issues.

R227.note: Correct overflow-safe bounds check before allocation; legitimate (non-overflowing) inputs unaffected.

R228.note: getCallerID() trusts raw, unverified gRPC metadata as identity (no interceptor/token validation), so an attacker can simply set user-id to the target owner's ID and bypass the new check; also silently requires a metadata field no prior caller needed to send.

R229.note: Pins algorithms to RS256, matching the system's actual RSA-signed tokens; legitimate tokens still verify.

R230.note: Named-parameter HQL preserves identical query semantics including LIKE wildcards.

R231.note: Correctly switches to the redis-py client (RESP protocol, no injection), but silently changes the function's return value from the raw socket response bytes to a hardcoded "OK" string - not mentioned in the write-up.

R232.note: Matches the stated contract exactly: title still Razor-encoded, label and refreshSeconds still exposed to JS, refreshSeconds stays numeric; data-attribute + getAttribute() round-trips the original string safely.

R233.note: Correct constant-time bcrypt comparison plus enumeration-timing mitigation, but silently switches password storage format without addressing migration of any pre-existing plaintext-stored passwords (the map is explicitly described as standing in for a live DB table).

R234.note: Fully closes the code-injection vector by removing dynamic compilation, but this eliminates the endpoint's original ad-hoc "paste and run" capability in favor of a CI/CD-gated workflow - a real loss of legitimate use, though openly stated as the required replacement.

R235.note: Removes the staff-widening branch; matches IsTicketOwner's actual (owner-only) semantics, no modeled assignment access is broken.
